title: Agent Evaluation & Monitoring in Production
description: Define agent success metrics, implement distributed tracing for agent loops, and set up real-time observability dashboards using OpenTelemetry and Azure Monitor.

data.text: Traditional ML metrics (accuracy, precision, recall) don't capture agent quality. An agent might produce correct answers but take too many steps, use too many tokens, or make unnecessary tool calls. Agent evaluation requires task-specific metrics: goal completion rate, step efficiency, tool call accuracy, hallucination rate, and user satisfaction.

rows: End-of-session user rating or outcome check
Percentage of tool calls that return useful results
Percentage of responses with factual errors
Percentage of sessions timing out (>30s per step)

data.text: Distributed Tracing for Agent Decision Chains

Each agent iteration (reason -> act -> observe) should be a trace span. When an agent calls multiple tools, each tool call is a child span. This creates a trace tree that reveals where time is spent, which tools are invoked, and why the agent took a particular path. OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for GenAI provide standardized attributes.

data.content: Instrumenting agent execution with structured trace spans:

data.text: Always use sampling — don't evaluate every single agent run. Sample traces and metrics at 100% for failed sessions, 10% for successful ones. Sampling all traces generates enormous cost and volume. Use head-based sampling for traces and tail-based sampling for alerting.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Agent metrics must capture step efficiency, tool accuracy, and token consumption — not just outcome
Use OpenTelemetry counters for aggregate metrics and histograms for distributions
Trace each agent step as a span; tool calls as child spans with GenAI semantic conventions
Implement sampling strategies to reduce observability cost at scale
Correlate traces with user feedback for closed-loop agent improvement
data.takeaway: Agent observability requires custom metrics and tracing beyond standard APM. Measure the agent's decision-making process, not just its final answer.
